overview: The Medford School Committee recognized outstanding student achievements, reviewed the Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility annual report, and voted to fund a student's travel to a national science conference if private sponsorship is not secured.

items.title: Approval of Minutes, Bills, and Payrolls
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes of October 15, 2018, accepted the payment of bills following discussion on athletic contracted services, and approved the district payrolls.

items.title: Superintendent's Report
items.summary: Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent reported on district activities and detailed a joint police investigation that cleared high school grounds after a single spent 9mm bullet casing was found on the athletic field.

items.title: Report on Student Backpack Donation Drive
items.summary: The committee presented certificates of appreciation to students Orlando and Isabella Putnam Bagley for collecting supplies and packing 101 backpacks for Andrews Middle School and Brooks Elementary School students.

items.title: Report on Massachusetts Junior Academy of Science Symposium
items.summary: The committee commended senior Subhashra Durali for her award-winning research on muscle hemodynamics and voted to cover her national conference expenses if corporate sponsorship is not obtained.

items.title: Report on Center for Citizenship and Social Responsibility
items.summary: Director Richard Trotta, coordinator Michael Skorka, and student leaders presented the 2017–2018 CCSR annual report and highlighted ongoing student-led community service projects.

items.title: Report on MHS/VTHS College Fair
items.summary: Director of Guidance Amelia Jensen reported on the 2018 College Fair, which hosted 99 post-secondary institutions alongside a specialized workshop on college transitions for students with IEPs and 504 plans.

items.title: Report on Elementary Highlights
items.summary: Associate Superintendent Diane Caldwell outlined recent elementary initiatives, including multicultural events, STEM fairs, and the Title I Bingo for Books program.

items.title: New Business and Condolences
items.summary: The committee passed resolutions of condolence for several local family members and observed a moment of silence for the victims of the synagogue shooting in Pittsburgh.
